mainTopic: How פסח שני differs from פסח ראשון, and which laws of the first פסח carry over to the second.
overview: The משנה lists how פסח שני differs from פסח ראשון: on פסח שני you may own חמץ, and no הלל is said at the meal. It also lists what the two share: הלל at the slaughter, eating the meat roasted with מצה and מרור, and overriding שבת. The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that only the מצוות of the קרבן itself carry over to פסח שני, along with מצה and מרור eaten with it. The ban on breaking a bone sets this limit. איסי בן יהודה learns the same limit from the words 'יעשו אותו'. The גמרא then shows how each side uses the other's words: 'עצם' teaches that every bone is included, and 'יעשו' teaches that a פסח is not slaughtered for one person alone. A second ברייתא shows that positive מצוות, fixable prohibitions, and full prohibitions of the קרבן all apply on פסח שני. The גמרא then reads each phrase of the פסוק as both including and excluding: roasting and 'לא תוציא' are included, while removing חמץ and בל יראה are excluded, because a מצוה of the קרבן itself is preferred. The same analysis of 'עצם לא ישברו בו' begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First difference: owning חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how פסח ראשון and פסח שני differ. The first difference: on פסח ראשון you may not own חמץ, but on פסח שני you may.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: What is the difference between the first פסח and the second? The first is subject to the prohibitions 'it shall not be seen' and 'it shall not be found.' On the second, a person may have חמץ and מצה with him in the house.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a question and gives its first answer. On פסח ראשון the laws of בל יראה and בל ימצא apply, but on פסח שני they do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסח שני is a make-up date for people who missed bringing the קרבן פסח. The משנה is telling us that the make-up date is only about the קרבן. It is not a full holiday, so the ban on owning חמץ does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the opening text being discussed)
The regular קרבן פסח on the 14th of ניסן
The make-up קרבן פסח on the 14th of אייר
The prohibition: חמץ shall not be seen in your possession
The prohibition: חמץ shall not be found in your possession
Leavened food

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think פסח שני is a one-week holiday like Pesach. It is only about bringing and eating the קרבן, so there is no week of חמץ restrictions.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
What is the difference between the first Pesach and the second?
The first is forbidden
under 'it shall not be seen' and 'it shall not be found,'
but on the second, chametz and matzah may be with him in the house.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: On פסח ראשון owning חמץ is forbidden. On פסח שני it is permitted.

steps.title: Second difference: הלל while eating
steps.stepSummary: On פסח ראשון you say הלל while eating the קרבן. On פסח שני you do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first requires הלל when it is eaten, and the second does not require הלל when it is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second difference between the two פסחים. It concerns saying הלל during the meal at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the night of פסח ראשון, the meal is eaten on a night of יום טוב, and הלל is sung with it. פסח שני has no יום טוב night, so there is no הלל at the meal.

keyTerms.meaning: Requires the recitation of הלל
At the time it is eaten

phrases.english: The first requires Hallel as it is eaten,
and the second does not require Hallel as it is eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second difference to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל is said at the meal of פסח ראשון, but not at the meal of פסח שני.

steps.title: What both פסח offerings share
steps.stepSummary: Both offerings need הלל while being slaughtered. Both are eaten roasted with מצה and מרור, and both override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both this one and that one require הלל when they are prepared. They are eaten roasted with מצה and bitter herbs, and they override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה switches from differences to similarities. It lists three ways that פסח שני is exactly like פסח ראשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything listed here is about the קרבן itself: how it is offered, how it is eaten, and the fact that it may be brought even on שבת. This hints at the rule the גמרא will teach. Laws about the קרבן carry over to פסח שני, and laws about the holiday do not.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one
When they are prepared, meaning when they are slaughtered
Roasted
Bitter herbs
They override שבת

steps.whatToRemember: Differences (חמץ, הלל at the meal) are holiday-related. Similarities (הלל at the slaughter, roasting, מצה and מרור, overriding שבת) are about the קרבן itself.

phrases.english: Both this and that require Hallel when they are prepared,
and they are eaten roasted with matzah and bitter herbs,
and they override Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from differences to the shared laws.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both offerings need הלל at the slaughter, are eaten roasted with מצה and מרור, and override שבת.

steps.title: Only laws of the offering itself carry over
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק 'ככל חוקת הפסח יעשו אותו' as referring only to the מצוות of the קרבן itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן taught: 'According to all the statute of the פסח they shall do it.' The verse is speaking about a מצוה of the offering's body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to find a source for the משנה's rules. The word 'אותו' (it) shows that the פסוק only means the laws of the animal itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read alone, 'all the statute of the Pesach' sounds like every law of Pesach applies on פסח שני. The ברייתא narrows it: 'do IT' means the laws done to the קרבן. Examples are roasting it and not leaving any meat over until morning.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
The רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)
The statute (laws) of the קרבן פסח
A מצוה done to the offering itself

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main principle that explains the entire משנה. Laws of the קרבן carry over to פסח שני. Laws of the holiday do not.

phrases.english: Gemara:
The Rabbis taught:
'According to all the statute of the Pesach they shall do it' —
the verse is speaking about a מצוה of its body.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן כְּכׇל חוּקַּת הַפֶּסַח יַעֲשׂוּ אוֹתוֹ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only מצוות שבגופו of the קרבן apply on פסח שני.

steps.title: What about laws attached to the offering?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for the source that מצוות eaten with the קרבן, like מצה and מרור, also apply on פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מצוה that is upon its body — from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a follow-up question and sets up the next step. We know the laws of the animal itself carry over, but what about things eaten together with it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: מצה and מרור are not done to the animal. They are eaten 'upon' it, as companions to it. The rule from the previous step might not include them, so a separate source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A מצוה attached to the offering (eaten with it), such as מצה and מרור
From where (is it derived)?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'שבגופו' (done to the animal itself) with 'שעל גופו' (eaten along with the animal). They differ by only one word.

phrases.english: A מצוה that is upon its body — from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the question to a second category of מצוה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that מצה and מרור eaten with the קרבן apply on פסח שני.

steps.title: Matzah and maror are stated explicitly
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about פסח שני itself says 'they shall eat it with מצות and מרורים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'With מצות and bitter herbs they shall eat it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question with a פסוק. It is written directly about פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Numbers 9:11 openly says that the פסח שני offering is eaten with מצה and מרור. So no special reading is needed: the Torah states it outright. This is the source for the משנה's line 'eaten roasted with מצה and מרור.'

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (introduces a source)
They shall eat it

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
'With matzot and bitter herbs they shall eat it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר עַל מַצּוֹת וּמְרוֹרִים יֹאכְלוּהוּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק explicitly requires מצה and מרור with the פסח שני offering.

steps.title: Maybe even unrelated laws apply?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a possibility: perhaps even מצוות not connected to the קרבן at all, like removing חמץ, apply on פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think that even מצוות that are not upon its body apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistaken idea (הוה אמינא), and the next step will rule it out. If 'all the statute' includes things eaten with the קרבן, maybe it includes everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the law reached beyond the animal itself to מצה and מרור, you might think there is no limit. That would include holiday laws like בל יראה. The ברייתא now needs a source to set a boundary.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (introduces a possibility to be rejected)
Not connected to the offering at all

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ מִצְוֹת שֶׁלֹּא עַל גּוּפוֹ —
phrases.english: One might think even מצוות that are not upon its body —

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ מִצְוֹת שֶׁלֹּא עַל גּוּפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the extension should go even further.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether laws unrelated to the קרבן, such as removing חמץ, also apply on פסח שני.

steps.title: Breaking a bone sets the limit
steps.stepSummary: The ban on breaking a bone is a law of the animal itself. From this example we learn that only laws of the קרבן apply on פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And they shall not break a bone in it.' Just as breaking a bone is distinctive in being a מצוה of its body, so too every מצוה of its body applies.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the possibility from the previous step. It uses the example of breaking a bone to limit פסח שני to laws of the קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק for פסח שני lists a specific example, the ban on שבירת עצם, which is done to the animal itself. From this example we learn the category: only that type of law carries over. So laws unrelated to the קרבן, like בל יראה, do not apply, just as the משנה said.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaking a bone of the offering
Just as ... so too (draws a comparison from an example)
Distinctive (in having a specific feature)

steps.whatToRemember: פסח שני includes: (1) laws of the animal itself, and (2) מצה and מרור eaten with it. It does not include holiday laws like removing חמץ.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'And they shall not break a bone in it,'
just as breaking a bone is distinctive
as a מצוה of its body —
so too every מצוה of its body.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר וְעֶצֶם לֹא יִשְׁבְּרוּ בוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the possibility raised in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The example of שבירת עצם limits פסח שני to laws of the קרבן itself. Unrelated laws are excluded.

steps.title: איסי בן יהודה: the word 'it' is enough
steps.stepSummary: איסי בן יהודה learns the same limit from the words 'יעשו אותו' instead of from the example of breaking a bone.
steps.simpleTranslation: איסי בן יהודה says: 'They shall do it' — the verse is speaking about מצוות of its body.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא gives a different source for the same rule. He says the word 'אותו' (it) already limits פסח שני to laws of the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא needed the bone example to set the limit. איסי בן יהודה says the phrase 'they shall do IT' already does that job. Both views reach the same law; they differ only in which words of the פסוק teach it.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who gives an alternate derivation
They shall do it (perform the offering)

phrases.english: Isi ben Yehuda says:
'They shall do it' —
the verse is speaking about מצוות of its body.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיסִי בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר יַעֲשׂוּ אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the limit set in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'אותו' itself limits פסח שני to מצוות שבגופו.

steps.title: How could anyone think unrelated מצוות apply?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's suggestion that even מצוות not on the body of the קרבן might apply on פסח שני. It challenges this, because the ברייתא already said the פסוק speaks only of מצוות on the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'Maybe even a מצוה not connected to the body of the קרבן applies.' But you already said the verse is talking about מצוות on its body! So how could you suggest that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the ברייתא and points out that it seems to contradict itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the ברייתא said 'יעשו אותו' limits פסח שני to מצוות of the animal itself. Then it suggested that even unrelated מצוות might apply. The גמרא asks why that suggestion was even possible after the limit was already stated.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said.' The phrase used to re-quote an earlier ברייתא or teaching in order to analyze it.
A מצוה connected to the body of the קרבן itself.
A מצוה not connected to the קרבן itself, like removing חמץ.
'But you said.' Points out that something was already stated.

phrases.english: The Master said:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אַף מִצְוָה שֶׁלֹּא עַל גּוּפוֹ.
phrases.english: One might think: even a מצוה not related to its body.
But you said
that the verse speaks of a מצוה related to its body?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אָמְרַתְּ בְּמִצְוָה שֶׁבְּגוּפוֹ הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא's suggestion in step 7 and challenges how that suggestion fits with the limit from 'יעשו אותו'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's suggestion that unrelated מצוות like removing חמץ might apply on פסח שני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא already said the פסוק deals only with מצוות on the body of the קרבן. So the suggestion seems to have no basis.

steps.title: Once מצה and מרור were added, a broad reading became possible
steps.stepSummary: Since the פסוק adds מצה and מרור, 'יעשו אותו' is not strictly limiting. The structure of the פסוק (details, then a general phrase) could then include every מצוה. So the example of breaking a bone is needed to limit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא means. Now that you said 'with מצות and מרורים they shall eat it,' we see that 'they shall perform it' is not an exact limit. So you might say the verse is a case of details followed by a general rule, where the general rule adds to the details and includes everything. So the bone example comes to teach us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא's suggestion was reasonable after all, and why the bone example was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מצה and מרור are not part of the animal itself. Since the פסוק includes them anyway, 'יעשו אותו' cannot be a strict limit. The פסוק lists details (מצה, מרור, leaving nothing over) and then says 'ככל חקת הפסח' (a general phrase). By the rule of פרט וכלל, a general phrase that comes after details includes everything, even removing חמץ. Breaking a bone, a law of the animal itself, is what sets the limit.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it means.' Introduces a re-explanation of a text.
Not exact; not meant as a strict limit.
A rule for reading the Torah: details listed first, followed by a general phrase.
The general phrase adds to the details and widens the law.
'It teaches us.' Shows what a source comes to exclude or include.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think מצה and מרור are מצוות 'on the body' of the animal in the strict sense. That is exactly why they show that 'יעשו אותו' is not an exact limit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the ברייתא needed the bone example at all. Without it, the general phrase would have pulled every law of the first פסח into פסח שני.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
Now that you said
"with matzos and bitter herbs they shall eat it,"
apparently "they shall perform it" is not an exact limit.
So say it is like a detail followed by a generalization,
and the generalization adds to the detail,
and includes even everything as well,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by re-reading the ברייתא's logic.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-explanation of the ברייתא's reasoning (הכי קאמר).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since מצה and מרור are included, 'יעשו אותו' is not exact. Then 'ככל חקת הפסח' as a כלל after a פרט would include all מצוות, even removing חמץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: The example of breaking a bone, a law of the animal itself, limits פסח שני to מצוות of the קרבן.

steps.title: What does איסי בן יהודה do with the word 'bone'?
steps.stepSummary: איסי בן יהודה learns the limit from 'יעשו אותו', not from the bone example. So the גמרא asks what he learns from the word 'עצם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And איסי בן יהודה, what does he do with this word 'bone'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what איסי בן יהודה does with the word 'עצם', since he did not use it to set the limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes every word in the Torah teaches something. איסי בן יהודה used 'יעשו אותו' for the limit, so the word 'עצם' seems to have no job. The גמרא asks what it teaches him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What does he do with it?' Asks how a sage uses a word he did not use for the main lesson.
Bone. Here, from the פסוק 'ועצם לא ישברו בו' (they shall not break a bone in it).

phrases.english: Isi ben Yehuda,
what does he do with this word "bone"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on איסי בן יהודה's different source from step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What איסי בן יהודה learns from the word 'עצם', since he did not use it for the limit.

steps.title: 'Bone' includes bones with and without marrow
steps.stepSummary: איסי בן יהודה uses 'עצם' to teach that the ban on breaking a bone applies to every bone, whether it has marrow or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it to teach: both a bone that has marrow and a bone that has no marrow are included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that איסי בן יהודה uses 'עצם' for its own lesson about which bones are included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the ban covers only bones with marrow inside, since those have something worth breaking them open for. The word 'עצם' teaches that every bone is included. So the word is not wasted for איסי בן יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He needs it for.' Shows that a word is used for a different lesson.
Marrow, the soft material inside a bone.

phrases.english: He needs it
to include both a bone that has marrow
and a bone that has no marrow.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְאֶחָד עֶצֶם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מוֹחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: איסי בן יהודה uses 'עצם' to include all bones, with or without marrow, in the ban on breaking a bone.

steps.title: What do the רבנן do with 'they shall perform it'?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn the limit from the bone example. So the גמרא asks what they learn from 'יעשו אותו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with this phrase 'they shall perform it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the opposite question: what the רבנן do with the words איסי בן יהודה used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side used a different phrase for the same limit. Now the גמרא checks that the רבנן also have a use for 'יעשו אותו', so no word is left without a lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis; the majority of sages, who disagree with איסי בן יהודה here.
'They shall perform it.' The phrase from the פסוק about פסח שני.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis,
what do they do with this phrase "they shall perform it"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן הַאי יַעֲשׂוּ אֹתוֹ מַאי עָבְדִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 12, this time asking about the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן learn from 'יעשו אותו', since they used the bone example for the limit.

steps.title: No פסח slaughtered for one person if others can be found
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use the plural 'יעשו' to teach that a פסח is not slaughtered for a single person. We must search for others to join him as much as possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it to teach that we do not slaughter the פסח for one individual alone. As much as it is possible to look for more people, we look.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן learn from the plural word 'יעשו' that a פסח should be brought by a group, not by one person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יעשו' means 'they shall perform,' which is plural. So the רבנן learn that one person should not bring a פסח alone. As long as we can find others to join him, we must search for them. This way both phrases in the פסוק are used by both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: We slaughter.
A single individual.
We search; we go looking (for more people).

steps.whatToRemember: איסי בן יהודה learns the limit from 'יעשו אותו' and uses 'עצם' to include every bone. The רבנן learn the limit from 'עצם' and use 'יעשו אותו' to teach that a פסח is not slaughtered for one person if others can be found.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical rule: a person bringing a פסח alone must first try to find others to join him.

phrases.english: They need it

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח עַל הַיָּחִיד,
phrases.english: to teach that we do not slaughter the Pesach for an individual,
for as much as it is possible to search for others, we search.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ שֶׁאֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח עַל הַיָּחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 and completes the picture of how both sides use the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural 'יעשו' teaches that a פסח is not slaughtered for a single person. We must search for others to join him whenever possible.

steps.title: A ברייתא: פסח שני has no ban on owning חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes 'ככל חוקת הפסח יעשו אותו'. It considers that פסח שני might have בל יראה and בל ימצא, and rejects this from 'על מצות ומרורים יאכלוהו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'According to all the laws of the פסח they shall do it.' You might think that just as on the first פסח it is forbidden to have חמץ (בל יראה and בל ימצא), so too on פסח שני it is forbidden. So the Torah says: 'With מצות and מרורים they shall eat it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. It explains which laws of the first פסח carry over to פסח שני. Its first point is that the ban on owning חמץ does not carry over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'ככל חוקת הפסח' sounds like it brings in every law of the first פסח. But the Torah names 'מצות ומרורים', which are tied to eating the קרבן. That shows the phrase covers laws connected to the קרבן itself, not the general holiday ban on owning חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)
The ban on letting your חמץ be seen on פסח
The ban on letting your חמץ be found in your possession on פסח
'You might think': raises a possible mistaken idea
'So the verse teaches': brings the פסוק that answers

steps.confusionAlert: פסח שני still has מצה and מרור with the קרבן. What it lacks is the ban on owning חמץ in your house. Eating מצה and owning no חמץ are two separate laws.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"According to all the statute of the Pesach they shall do it."
One might think: just as on the first one it is forbidden
under "it shall not be seen" and "it shall not be found"
so too on the second one it is forbidden
under "it shall not be seen" and "it shall not be found"
Therefore the verse teaches:
"With matzot and bitter herbs they shall eat it."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כְּכׇל חוּקַּת הַפֶּסַח יַעֲשׂוּ אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא on the same topic as the earlier discussion of 'יעשו אותו'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban of בל יראה and בל ימצא does not apply on פסח שני.

steps.title: Where do we learn that prohibitions also carry over?
steps.stepSummary: The example 'מצות ומרורים' is a מצות עשה. The ברייתא asks where we learn that negative commandments also carry over, and answers from 'לא ישאירו ממנו עד בקר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: From this I only know about a positive מצוה. Where do I learn about a negative מצוה? The verse says: 'They shall not leave any of it until morning.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues building its list of examples. It shows that a לא תעשה, not leaving meat over until morning, also applies to פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating with מצה and מרור is a מצות עשה, so it could only teach about positive commandments. The פסוק also names a לאו, 'לא ישאירו'. This shows prohibitions are included too.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive commandment (something you must do)
A negative commandment (something you may not do)
From where do we learn it?
Meat of a קרבן left over past its time (the topic of 'לא ישאירו')

phrases.english: And I only have a positive מצוה;
from where do I know a negative מצוה?
The verse teaches:
"They shall not leave any of it until morning."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה, מִצְוַת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the example from a positive מצוה to a prohibition
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that negative commandments also apply to פסח שני

steps.title: Where do we learn that a full prohibition carries over?
steps.stepSummary: 'לא ישאירו' is a לאו שניתק לעשה. The ברייתא asks about a full לאו and answers from 'ועצם לא ישברו בו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: From this I only know about a prohibition that can be fixed by a positive מצוה. Where do I learn about a full prohibition? The verse says: 'And they shall not break a bone in it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a third type of example, a full prohibition: breaking a bone of the קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If meat is left over, there is a מצוה to burn it, so that לאו can be 'fixed'. That makes it a weaker kind of לאו, and it could not teach about a full לאו. Breaking a bone cannot be fixed, so it shows that full prohibitions also apply.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition that can be fixed by doing a positive מצוה afterward
A full prohibition that cannot be fixed afterward
Breaking a bone of the קרבן פסח

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא מִצְוַת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
phrases.english: And I only have a negative מצוה
that can be fixed by a positive מצוה.
From where do I know a full negative מצוה?
The verse teaches:
"And they shall not break a bone in it."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא מִצְוַת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁנִּיתָּק לַעֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a fixable prohibition to a full prohibition
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that a full לאו also applies to פסח שני

steps.title: From the three examples, every similar מצוה is included
steps.stepSummary: The three named examples (עשה, לאו שניתק לעשה, לאו גמור) show the pattern. The general phrase 'ככל חוקת' then includes every מצוה of these three types.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as the details are spelled out (a positive מצוה, a prohibition fixable by a positive מצוה, and a full prohibition), so too every positive מצוה, every fixable prohibition, and every full prohibition is included.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא wraps up. It uses the three examples as a model to include every מצוה of those same kinds in פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats the named details as a model ('מה הפרט מפורש'). The general phrase 'ככל חוקת' then includes only things like those details, not literally everything. Since the details cover all three kinds of מצוות, all three kinds carry over. Excluded are laws unlike them, such as removing חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: A detail or specific example in the פסוק
A general, all-including phrase in the פסוק
'Just as the detail is spelled out, so too everything like it'

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's bottom line: every מצוה of the קרבן פסח (עשה, fixable לאו, full לאו) applies on פסח שני too. But the ban on owning חמץ does not.

phrases.english: Just as the detail is spelled out:
a positive מצוה,
and a prohibition fixable by a positive מצוה,
and a full prohibition —
so too every positive מצוה,
and every prohibition fixable by a positive מצוה,
and every full prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the three examples to draw the general rule
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three kinds of מצוות of the קרבן carry over to פסח שני.

steps.title: What does 'מצות ומרורים' include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra law is included by the inclusive side of 'מצות ומרורים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Through the general side of 'מצות ומרורים', what does it include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now examines the phrase 'מצות ומרורים' on its own. It asks what this phrase adds, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase works in two directions: it includes laws like itself and excludes laws unlike itself. Here the גמרא asks about the including side, meaning which law tied to eating the קרבן it brings in.

keyTerms.meaning: Through its general (including) side
Includes, adds

phrases.english: Through the generalization of "matzot and bitter herbs,"
what does it include?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּכְלָלֵיהּ דְּמַצּוֹת וּמְרוֹרִים מַאי קָא מְרַבֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first example in the ברייתא and asks about its own function
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law the phrase 'מצות ומרורים' includes

steps.title: It includes roasting over fire
steps.stepSummary: The phrase includes צלי אש: the פסח שני must also be roasted over fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: Roasting over fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the phrase includes the law of roasting the קרבן over fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Roasting is about how the meat is prepared to be eaten, just like eating it with מצה and מרור. Because it matches, it is included.

keyTerms.meaning: Roasted over fire (how the קרבן פסח must be cooked)

phrases.english: Roasting in fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what is included
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: צלי אש applies to פסח שני

steps.title: What does 'מצות ומרורים' exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the limiting side of 'מצות ומרורים' excludes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Through its detail, what does it exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the other direction of the phrase: what it leaves out. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A specific detail also limits. It shows that only things like it are included, so something unlike it must be left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Through its detail (limiting) side
Excludes, limits

phrases.english: Through its detail, what does it exclude?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the mirror question to step 20
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law the phrase 'מצות ומרורים' excludes

steps.title: It excludes getting rid of חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The phrase excludes השבתת שאור, the duty to remove חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Removing leaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that getting rid of חמץ is not required on פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing חמץ from your house has nothing to do with how the קרבן is eaten. So it is left out, which matches the ברייתא's opening point about בל יראה and בל ימצא.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה to get rid of חמץ before פסח

phrases.english: Removal of leaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers what is excluded
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: השבתת שאור does not apply on פסח שני

steps.title: Why not reverse the two?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: perhaps reverse it, so that removing חמץ is included and roasting is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: I can reverse it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that we could just as easily swap the two: require removing חמץ and drop roasting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase both includes one thing and excludes another. The question is how we know which law goes on which side. Nothing so far explains the choice.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I will reverse it': a challenge asking why not swap the conclusion

phrases.english: I can reverse it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the split given in steps 21 and 23
steps.kashyaTarget: The assignment of צלי אש as included and השבתת שאור as excluded
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without a reason, the opposite assignment is equally possible.

steps.title: A מצוה of the קרבן itself is stronger
steps.stepSummary: A מצוה done to the קרבן itself (roasting) is more fitting to carry over than one outside it (removing חמץ).
steps.simpleTranslation: A מצוה of the body (of the קרבן) itself is preferable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that roasting is about the קרבן itself, so it is the one that carries over to פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסח שני is mainly about bringing the קרבן again. So laws done to the קרבן's own body are the natural ones to include. Removing חמץ is a separate holiday law, so it is the one excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: A מצוה done to the קרבן itself
Is preferable / stronger

steps.whatToRemember: On פסח שני, laws of the קרבן itself (like roasting it) apply. Holiday laws outside the קרבן (like getting rid of חמץ) do not.

phrases.english: A מצוה relating to the offering itself is preferable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'reverse it' challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical priority: the more closely connected law is the one included
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either law could be the included one
steps.terutzMaskana: Roasting, a law of the קרבן itself, is included; removing חמץ is excluded

steps.title: What does the general side of 'leave none of it until morning' include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which additional law is included by reading 'לא ישאירו ממנו עד בקר' as a general statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Through the general side of 'they shall leave none of it until morning', what law does the verse include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase in the פסוק about פסח שני. It asks what extra law this phrase brings in. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as with 'מצות ומרורים', each phrase does two jobs. As a כלל it pulls in a similar law that also applies on פסח שני. As a פרט it keeps out another law. This question is about the 'pulling in' side.

keyTerms.meaning: Through its general side (reading the phrase as a broad statement)
They shall leave none of it until morning (the ban on leftovers)
Includes, adds

phrases.aramaic: בִּכְלָלֵיהּ דְּ״לֹא יַשְׁאִירוּ מִמֶּנּוּ עַד בֹּקֶר״
phrases.english: Through the generalization of 'They shall leave none of it until morning'
what does it include?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּכְלָלֵיהּ דְּ״לֹא יַשְׁאִירוּ מִמֶּנּוּ עַד בֹּקֶר״ מַאי קָא מְרַבֵּה לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing 'מצות ומרורים', the גמרא applies the same include/exclude method to the next phrase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law of the first פסח is included for פסח שני through the general side of 'לא ישאירו'?

steps.title: It includes the ban on taking the meat out
steps.stepSummary: The phrase includes 'לא תוציא ממנו', the ban on taking the meat out of its place. Both bans make the meat invalid: one as נותר, the other as יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It includes 'You shall not take any of it out', which is similar to it. This one (leftovers) becomes invalid as נותר, and that one (taking out) becomes invalid as יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the general side of the phrase includes the ban on taking the קרבן's meat outside its group. It also explains why these two bans count as similar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both bans work the same way. Breaking either one makes the meat itself invalid. Leaving it overnight makes it נותר, and taking it out of its boundary makes it יוצא. Because they match like this, the leftovers ban can carry 'לא תוציא' along with it to פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not take any of it out (of the house or group)
Which is similar to it
Meat left past its allowed time, which makes it invalid
Meat taken outside its allowed boundary, which makes it invalid
Becomes invalid

phrases.english: 'You shall not take out any of it'
which is similar to it,
since this one becomes invalid as leftover,
and that one becomes invalid as having gone out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The general side includes לא תוציא, because like נותר it is a ban that makes the meat invalid.

steps.title: What does the specific side exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which law is left out by reading the same phrase as a specific detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: Through its specific side, what does it exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks about the second job of the phrase: what law it keeps away from פסח שני. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general side has already been explained. Now the specific side has to leave out some law that also looks similar to the leftovers ban.

keyTerms.meaning: Through its specific side (reading the phrase as a limited detail)
Excludes, leaves out

phrases.english: Through its detail,
what does it exclude?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the including side to the excluding side of the same phrase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law of the first פסח is excluded from פסח שני through the specific side of 'לא ישאירו'?

steps.title: It excludes the bans on owning חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The phrase excludes בל יראה ובל ימצא. They are similar to the leftovers ban because neither one brings lashes, since each is a לאו שניתק לעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It excludes 'It shall not be seen' and 'It shall not be found', which are similar to it. One who breaks this ban (leftovers) is not given lashes, because it is a ban that can be fixed by a positive מצוה. And one who breaks that ban (חמץ) is not given lashes, because it is also a ban that can be fixed by a positive מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the specific side leaves out the bans against owning חמץ, so they do not apply on פסח שני. It explains the way they resemble the leftovers ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leftovers ban and the חמץ bans share one feature. In both cases, breaking the ban can be fixed by doing a positive מצוה, which is burning the leftovers or destroying the חמץ. So neither one is punished with lashes. That shared feature makes בל יראה a good candidate for the specific side to exclude.

keyTerms.meaning: It shall not be seen and it shall not be found (the bans on owning חמץ)
Receives lashes
A ban whose violation can be fixed by doing a positive מצוה, so it brings no lashes

steps.confusionAlert: The two bans are NOT similar because they make something invalid. The likeness here is a different one: neither brings lashes. The גמרא uses one kind of likeness to include a law and a different kind of likeness to exclude one.

phrases.english: 'It shall not be seen and it shall not be found'
which is similar to it,
since this one does not receive lashes
because it is a ban that can be fixed by a positive command,
and that one does not receive lashes
because it is a ban that can be fixed by a positive command.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The specific side excludes בל יראה ובל ימצא, which resemble the leftovers ban since both are לאו שניתק לעשה.

steps.title: Why not switch which law is included and which is excluded?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: maybe include בל יראה and exclude לא תוציא instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: I can reverse it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the split it just made. Both laws resemble the leftovers ban, so it asks why we shouldn't swap them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the two laws has a real likeness to 'לא ישאירו'. Nothing in the reasoning so far shows which one belongs on the including side. So the swap seems just as valid.

keyTerms.meaning: I will reverse it (a challenge to switch the two sides)

phrases.english: I will reverse it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the include/exclude split from steps 27 and 29. This repeats the pattern of step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decision to include לא תוציא and exclude בל יראה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both laws have a likeness to the leftovers ban, so the assignment seems arbitrary and could be swapped.

steps.title: A מצוה about the קרבן itself is preferred
steps.stepSummary: Taking the meat out has to do with the קרבן itself, so it is the better law to include. חמץ has nothing to do with the קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מצוה of its own body is preferable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we include the law that deals with the קרבן itself. That law is the ban on taking the meat out. The ban on owning חמץ is not about the קרבן, so it is excluded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic is which laws of the פסח קרבן carry over to פסח שני. A rule about the קרבן's own meat fits that topic better than a rule about חמץ in your house. This is the same reasoning that settled the question in step 25.

keyTerms.meaning: A מצוה that concerns the קרבן itself
Is preferable, takes priority

steps.whatToRemember: From 'לא ישאירו': לא תוציא IS included in פסח שני, and בל יראה ובל ימצא is NOT. The tiebreaker each time is that a מצוה about the קרבן itself wins.

phrases.english: A command concerning its own body is preferable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30 with the same principle used in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Priority principle: a law about the קרבן itself wins over one outside it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The assignment could be swapped, so that בל יראה applies on פסח שני and לא תוציא does not.
steps.terutzMaskana: לא תוציא concerns the קרבן's meat, so it is the one included. בל יראה is excluded.

steps.title: Starting the next phrase: 'do not break a bone in it'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins asking what the general side of 'עצם לא ישברו בו' includes. The question finishes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Through the general side of 'they shall not break a bone in it'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next question, now about the last phrase, 'they shall not break a bone in it'. The rest of the question and the answer continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same two-sided method is now applied to the bone-breaking ban. The גמרא will ask which similar law it includes and which it excludes.

keyTerms.meaning: They shall not break a bone in it (the ban on breaking the פסח's bones)

phrases.english: Through the generalization of 'They shall not break a bone in it'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next phrase of the פסוק, using the same method as step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law is included through the general side of 'עצם לא ישברו בו'? The question is completed on the next amud.
